title: Gumroad
snippet:
## Scopes
We've provided the following scopes that you may request when the user authorizes your application.
**account:** full access to most API endpoints. Endpoints with a narrower security boundary, such as media, refuse an account-only token and require the specific scope noted on the endpoint.
**view_profile:** read-only access to the user's public information and products.
**edit_profile:** write access to the user's profile name and bio.
**edit_products:** read/write access to the user's products and their variants, offer codes, custom fields, and files.
**edit_emails:** read/write access to the user's audience emails and read access to the user's workflows.
**view_sales:** read access to the user's products' sales information, including sales counts. This scope is also required in order to subscribe to the user's sales.
**view_payouts:** read access to the user's payouts information.
**view_tax_data:** read access to the user's tax forms (1099-K, 1099-MISC) and annual earnings summary.
**mark_sales_as_shipped:** write access to mark the user's products' sales as shipped.
**edit_sales:** write access to refund the user's products' sales, revoke or restore buyer access, and resend purchase receipts to customers.

Gumroad's OAuth 2.0 API lets you see information about your products, as well as you can add, edit, and delete offer codes, variants, and custom fields. Finally, you can see a user's public information and subscribe to be notified of their sales.

snippet:
Gumroad has no subscription plans, which makes the usual question on a page like this unusually simple to answer. There is no Pro tier, no Business tier and no monthly bill, so there is no plan for API access to sit behind. Gumroad's published pricing is a per-transaction cut and nothing else: 10 percent plus 50 cents on sales through your own profile and direct links, and 30 percent when a new customer finds you through Gumroad's Discover marketplace. Any account can create an application, generate an access token and call the API immediately. Nothing on this page is gated behind an upgrade, and there is no free tier exclusion list to read, because there is no paid tier to be excluded from.

## Connecting Gumroad takes one credential
Gumroad issues access tokens from its own account settings rather than from a separate developer portal: open Settings, then Advanced, and use the application form there. You create an application, then generate an access token for your own account from it, which is the credential this connector takes. There is no purchase step and no review queue in front of it, because Gumroad sells no plans and gates nothing here behind billing. One thing to get right before you build: Gumroad's scopes are not a formality. Its reference lists ten of them, account, view_profile, edit_profile, edit_products, edit_emails, view_sales, view_payouts, view_tax_data, mark_sales_as_shipped and edit_sales, and states that account gives full access to most endpoints while endpoints with a narrower security boundary, such as media, refuse an account only token and require the specific scope named on the endpoint. Every node in this connector names the scope its endpoint documents, because a missing scope is the most likely reason a correctly built workflow fails, and it fails as a refusal on a token that looks fully privileged.

title: Create an application for the API - Gumroad Help Center
snippet:
If you're writing some custom code you need to run with your Gumroad account, all you need is an access token. Your access token is used in the request header of every request to the API and should be kept secret, like a password.

- **Redirect URI:** While this is very important when making a general-purpose application, when you just want an access token to use the API with your own account, simply enter localhost (http://127.0.0.1) in this field, as its value is not meaningful.

When you make an API call, include it in the request's header. Here's an example of a request with the access token (replace ACCESS_TOKEN with the string from your application):
```
curl https://api.gumroad.com/v2/products \-d "access_token=ACCESS_TOKEN" \-X GET
```

| Env var | Secret | Format | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GUMROAD_ACCESS_TOKEN` | secret | `opaque token string (shape only)` | Access token for your own Gumroad account; does not expire until revoked. |
| `GUMROAD_APPLICATION_ID` | not secret | `opaque id string` | OAuth application id (client id). |
| `GUMROAD_APPLICATION_SECRET` | secret | `opaque secret string (shape only)` | OAuth application secret (server side only). |

After creating an application, you'll be given a unique application id and application secret.
On the application page, click **Generate access token** to get the token you will use with the API.

- **view_sales:** read access to the user's products' sales information, including sales counts. This scope is also required in order to subscribe to the user's sales.
